judgment.rationale: Both are Performance Objectives in the same PRIMARY THREE Topic '1. Symmetry' / Sub-Theme 'Shapes'. First objective 4 asks pupils to identify square, rectangular, triangular and circular shapes in everyday life; second objective 3 asks pupils to state properties of squares, rectangles and triangles. They share substantive conceptual coherence about the same shape families (squares, rectangles, triangles) and mutually reinforce each other—recognising shapes and describing their properties are complementary geometry skills. However, both sit at the same grade rank (2) and the evidence does not clearly establish a single developmental direction: identification could support property statement, yet the source numbering lists property-stating (obj 3) before everyday identification (obj 4), leaving direction ambiguous. Symmetric relatesTo best fits the coherence without asserting an unsupported dependency direction.
